Q: Excel formula calculating working hours depending on shift start and shift end A:

You can use the MOD function to pull out the time part of the datetime.

Example: Assume your data is as follows:

       A                       B
   1   02/06/2023 3:00 PM      =((A5-MOD(A1,1))*24)+((MOD(A2,1)-A4)*24) ~~> 14.00
   2   12/07/2023 8:00 PM
   3
   4   11:00 AM
   5   8:00 AM

In B1 add the formula =((A5-MOD(A1,1))*24)+((MOD(A2,1)-A4)*24) and it will return 14, the number of hours worked (i.e. 5 + 9).

Hope this helps

Q: What does git checkout do? A:

  • Running git checkout -- <file> (without a commit specified) copies the file from the index to the working tree, leaving your staging area untouched.

  • Running git checkout <commit> -- <file> copies the file from that specific commit into both the index and the working tree.

The index is updated to match the version of hello.txt present in commit 11cb5b6. Because that version now differs from your current HEAD commit, Git registers it as a staged modification ready to be committed.

Modern Git (v2.23+) splits these actions into:

  • git switch for changing branches.

  • git restore for files, where you can explicitly choose whether to update the worktree (--worktree), the index (--staged), or both.
